title: lmvideo books
description: Learn to draw images, build scenes and render video with authored examples and locally verified showcases.

groups.title: Getting started
groups.summary: Install the command runner, read a script and generate your first image.

blocks.text: Install the lmctl command runner with npm install -g @lmctl-ai/lmctl. Read the source before running downloaded programs, then use a fresh directory for outputs. This first example uses a released lmvideo host declared by its source.

groups.title: CPU Cycles
groups.summary: Render the same authored scene with a CPU path tracer, as a still and a video.

blocks.text: Raster is the fast preview path. The same scene can use CPU Cycles for final lighting, reflections and roughness. A Cycles-enabled lmvideo binary and matching module must be installed locally; this candidate is not a published installable release.

Save each displayed source at its named examples/book/ path before running its compile/render commands. The output below is the structured result from the locked chapter capture; timing fields describe that historical run and vary on another machine.

blocks.alt: A 960 by 540 CPU Cycles still with denoising.
blocks.caption: A 960 by 540 CPU Cycles still with denoising.
Forty-eight frames rendered by CPU Cycles at 24 frames per second. The still above is the chapter poster, not a frame from the clip.

blocks.text: The seven render_image arguments are width, height, renderer name, samples, maximum bounces, repeatable seed and denoise. A build without Cycles must report an error rather than silently render with raster. Video generation compiles once and renders each frame; these captures are local verification evidence, not a new website benchmark run.
